text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.45% today to $457.22, continuing a five-day decline that has shed $21 from its October 16 high. The sell-off comes despite Brent crude oil hitting $116 per barrel—a six-month high—driven by escalating Middle East tensions and Trump administration threats of strikes against Iran. For a refiner, higher crude prices typically squeeze profit margins on fuel production, which appears to be outweighing any benefit from the elevated oil prices themselves.

The broader refining environment supports this squeeze: U.S. refineries are running at 93.4% capacity while gasoline and diesel inventories remain well-stocked, meaning refiners can't easily pass higher crude costs to consumers. As geopolitical risk keeps crude elevated, refiners face the worst scenario—forced to buy expensive raw material into a market where they can't command higher margins on the finished fuel they sell.
